thought.text: The LDAP test users weren't loaded. Let me inspect the bootstrap mount and reset as the guide suggests.

reasoning_content:
The test users were not loaded because on this startup, the database already existed (from first attempt) and bootstrap ldif only loads on first init. Also the custom ldif was mounted and processed initially? Let's check the earlier log: "Add custom bootstrap ldif..." failed at sed. Then we restarted with dir mount, but database was empty? Actually the second attempt created DB and then failed at the sed. Third attempt with dir mount: "Database and config directory are empty... Init new ldap server" then later failed at "rm cannot remove custom". Fourth attempt with REMOVE_CONFIG false: it said "First start is done..." meaning it already had data? Hmm, let me check if DB now has data but no users.

Actually the LDAP volume now contains the base DN but no users. The custom ldif may not have been added. Let me check the ldap-bootstrap dir - maybe it was sed-processed and renamed.

Wait, on the 4th restart, the log says "First start is done..." which means it detected existing data and didn't re-init. But the data was created in the 3rd attempt before it failed at rm? In the 3rd attempt, database was empty, it re-initialized, added bootstrap schemas, added image bootstrap ldif, then "Add custom bootstrap ldif" -> sed and then rm failure. Actually the rm failure was in "Remove config files" which happens after. So custom ldif should have been added. But ldapsearch shows no people OU.

Hmm, maybe the custom ldif was sed'd with wrong domain. The osixia image seds the ldif to replace domain. Let me check the mount contents.

Actually wait — the 3rd attempt: it failed at "rm: cannot remove '.../custom': Device or resource busy" during "Remove config files". That happens after setup completes. But did it add custom ldif? The log showed earlier lines. Let me re-run a fresh LDAP by resetting volumes to ensure users load. Guide says: use `ddev delete --omit-snapshot -y` to reset LDAP volumes.

But first let me check the current state of the mounted dir - the sed creates a temp file then renames; with a directory mount that works.

Let me just do the documented volume reset: ddev delete --omit-snapshot -y then ddev start. But careful: ddev delete removes database too, so I'd need to re-import the dump. The guide says that's the LDAP reset procedure. Let's do it.

Actually, let me first verify whether users are truly missing vs. the search base. The base is dc=example,dc=org. Only 1 entry (the root). So yes users missing.

Let me check the bootstrap ldif processing. Maybe the custom file in the mounted dir got renamed/modified. Let me look.

action.command: cd /workspace; ls -la .ddev/ldap-bootstrap/; echo "=== container custom dir ==="; docker exec ddev-tfm-fachplanung-openldap bash -c 'ls -la /container/service/slapd/assets/config/bootstrap/ldif/custom/ 2>&1; echo "---content---"; head -30 /container/service/slapd/assets/config/bootstrap/ldif/custom/*.ldif 2>&1'
